note: Re-judged 2026-10-26 at HEAD dfabdcf8bf (independent judge, clean clone), after 3c8b9e42de, dd20e0aa1a and dfabdcf8bf. RFC 3948 Section 5.1: "Because SGW will now see two possible SAs that lead to 10.1.2.3, it can become confused about where to send packets coming from Suzy's server.  Implementors MUST devise ways of preventing this from occurring." THE EARLIER FINDING IS FIXED: TestInnerSelectorInstallBackstopRefusesSecond (two responders that both passed narrowing, second install refused TS_UNACCEPTABLE with the conflict fix, nothing on its dataplane) and TestInnerSelectorInitiatorInstallRefusedInstallsNothing (an initiator install from an adopted answer refused, nothing installed) are now tagged negative. Probe in the clone (go -overlay, tree untouched), tagged set only: claim's conflictLocked disabled -> exactly those two go red; installChildSA's claim result ignored -> the same two red; operatorOrdered -> return true -> TestRFC3948ConfiguredOverlapEqualPriorityRefused red (both 2000 and both unset); releaseInnerRecord always releasing -> TestRFC3948FailedPolicyRemovalKeepsRecord red (EIO keeps the record and refuses peer b; ENOENT, ErrNotSupported, PolicyOwnedError and EPROTONOSUPPORT release it); newChildSA's registry assignment dropped -> seven tagged units red. With the narrowing filter disabled the tagged set stays green, correctly: the install backstop still answers TS_UNACCEPTABLE, so compliance holds. Distinct-priority operator overlaps stay legal under RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1 "Thus, a user or administrator MUST be able to order the entries to express a desired access control policy." The pool-bound path keeps its records (assignVirtualIP, substituteVirtualIP, proposeChildTSPayloads, answerNamesOnlyLeases). WHY STILL WEAK: every tagged unit builds its SA by hand and assigns sa.innerSelectors itself, and none rekeys, so the guard's reach from a real session and across a rekey is unproven. Probe, whole engine package: (1) newRekeyedChild (rekey.go) dropping innerGuard: old.innerGuard -> all ten tagged units PASS, only the untagged TestInnerSelectorSamePeerRekeyAllowed goes red. Scenario: peer a holds 10.1.2.3/32; its Child SA rekeys (hourly by default); the replacement carries a zero guard, so claim records nothing; the retired Child SA's removal releases a's record; peer b proposing 10.1.2.3/32 is then admitted and two SAs lead to 10.1.2.3. (2) the session wiring: deleting sa.innerSelectors = ps.innerSelectors in register.go (responder SA), in fsm.go (initiator SA), the innerSelectors: table.innerSelectors line in reconcile.go (PeerSession), or the innerSelectors: oldSA.innerSelectors inheritance in rekey.go (both IKE SA rekey paths) -> the WHOLE engine package passes in each case. With any of them gone a production SA carries no registry, dropForeignInnerOverlaps returns every pair and innerSelectorGuard.claim records nothing, so two peers hold one inner address; only the untagged interop scenario unbound-inner-address-uniqueness (requireOneInnerTunnel, internal/le/interoplab/ipsec/unbound_inner.go) reaches the responder wiring, and nothing reaches the IKE SA rekey inheritance. Fix: add a negative unit test, tagged RFC3948-5.1-1, in which peer a's Child SA rekeys (respondChildRekey and the Ze-initiated rekey), the retired Child SA is removed, and peer b proposing a's inner address is refused TS_UNACCEPTABLE, with a record on newRekeyedChild's innerGuard line; and a negative test driving two peer sessions built from one SATable (reconcile.go session constructor) through handleInit/IKE_AUTH and an IKE SA rekey, with records on the register.go, fsm.go, reconcile.go and rekey.go assignments, or tag the interop checker requireOneInnerTunnel with its record. The code meets the requirement as read (every assignment is present at HEAD), so the Support remaining text is not false; its proof is mechanism-level, not entry-point-level.
